source.title: Image Classification at Supercomputer Scale
source.authors: Chris Ying; Sameer Kumar; Dehao Chen; Tao Wang; You-Long Cheng

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how batch normalization batch size and large-batch training choices affect ImageNet validation accuracy, refining the large-batch generalization-gap claim. Its other experiments concern throughput rather than the claim.
record.gate_note: Only the distributed batch-normalization experiment reports outcomes relevant to held-out accuracy. The input-pipeline and gradient-summation results concern throughput; prior-work claims in Related Work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study's own Table 1 compares ResNet-50 ImageNet validation accuracy across global batch sizes and training recipes, all trained for 90 epochs. These results test V5's large-batch penalty and its qualification that an adapted recipe can preserve accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the combined systems and training recipe achieves 76.3% ImageNet validation accuracy in 2.2 minutes on 1024 TPU v3 chips. Distributed BN decouples its statistics batch size from global batch size; combined with LARS, it enables this scale without an accuracy drop.
record.recipe_differences: Large-batch ResNet-50 ImageNet training with distributed batch normalization, learning-rate scaling, warmup and decay, and LARS in some runs; not a controlled fixed-epoch comparison of global batch sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Effective batch-normalization size/group size changes validation accuracy and training time. The text states that per-core batch size below 32 causes a big drop in model performance; increasing group size raises training time.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed global batch size, effective BN batch size 16 produces a substantial validation-performance drop.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ImageNet ResNet-50 validation accuracy depends on the number of examples used to estimate batch-normalization statistics, independently of global training batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing distributed BN group size increases total training time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distributed batch-normalization statistics incur additional communication and computation costs as group size increases.

record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: Figure 6 contains the accuracy and time values without numerical values in the text. The reported experiments vary group size/effective BN batch size, not global batch size under a fixed epoch budget, so they do not directly test the central fixed-epoch comparison in V5.
record.rows_left_out: Input-pipeline additions/ablations and gradient-summation comparisons in Figures 5 and 7 report throughput or time, not held-out accuracy or train-test generalization. Table 1's other accuracy comparisons are state-of-the-art results, not controlled experiments isolating the claim's variables.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under the specified tuning protocols.
Language models, longer-training remedies, and separate causal contributions of learning-rate scaling, warmup, LARS, normalization, and label smoothing.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Own 90-epoch baseline and momentum result: batch 1024, local BN, 76.3%; batch 16384, local BN, 75.3%. The record incorrectly dismisses the relevant Table 1 comparisons as other studies' results.
missing.locator: Section 5 and Table 1, Baseline and first Ours row

missing.what: Own 90-epoch LARS results: batch 32768 with local BN reaches 76.3% on TPU v2 and 76.4% on TPU v3; batch 65536 with local BN reaches 75.2%; batch 32768 with distributed BN reaches 76.3%. These establish both successful adaptation and a remaining larger-batch penalty, without isolating each recipe component.
missing.locator: Section 5 and Table 1, remaining Ours rows

record.verdict_notes: The record's assertion that no fixed-epoch global-batch comparison is reported is incorrect: Section 5 explicitly specifies 90 epochs. Table 1 contains both cited results and the authors' own baseline and experiments. Those own results are essential despite the record's blanket exclusion. The paper is not an original source for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.

No comparison of batch sizes at a fixed epoch budget in the reported experiments; results instead vary effective batch-normalization size and report training time alongside validation accuracy. It does not test language models or whether longer training closes a gap.
Sharpness or other measured properties as predictors of the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train with effective batch-normalization size 16 (group size 1)
rows.note: Text says the baseline reaffirms that a per-core batch size below 32 causes a big drop in model performance; exact accuracy is shown only in the figure.
rows.check: This measures an accuracy loss from a small batch-normalization statistics batch while global batch size is fixed. It cannot establish V5's penalty from increasing the global training batch.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train with distributed batch normalization at effective batch-normalization size 64 (group size 4)
rows.measure: ImageNet validation accuracy and total training time
rows.note: Authors select effective BN batch size 64 based on these experiments; exact accuracy and time are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Relevant to V5's normalization adaptation component, but the supplied figure has no readable values. Selecting BN size 64 does not by itself establish how much accuracy is recovered or whether the global-batch penalty disappears. Separate validation accuracy from training time; remove the spurious extracted number 1/1.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train with effective batch-normalization sizes across a range of group sizes
rows.baseline: group size 1 / effective BN batch size 16
rows.note: The text explicitly reports increased training time as the cost of computing group mean and variance rises.
rows.check: Training time alone does not measure V5's held-out performance penalty. This is a systems-cost result, not evidence that the generalization effect is partial; remove the spurious extracted number 1/1.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50 on ImageNet, 90 epochs, momentum with global batch 16384 or LARS with global batch 65536, local BN
relationships.reason: Table 1, missing from the rows, reports 75.3% and 75.2% accuracy respectively, below the batch-1024 baseline's 76.3%; recipe and hardware differences prevent attributing the entire difference to batch size.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified comparisons suggest lower accuracy at the larger batches, with recipe and hardware differences preventing isolated batch-size attribution.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50 on ImageNet, 90 epochs, global batch 32768 with LARS and the adapted training recipe
relationships.reason: Table 1, missing from the rows, reports 76.3–76.4% with local BN and 76.3% with distributed BN, matching or exceeding the batch-1024 baseline's 76.3%, supporting V5's same-budget adaptation qualification.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest the adapted batch-32768 recipes matched or exceeded the smaller-batch reference within the same epoch budget.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-50 on ImageNet, varying effective BN batch size with per-core batch size 16 on a TPU v2 Pod
reader_labels.reason: The per-core batch size below 32 is reported to cause a big validation-performance drop, while grouping replicas permits an effective BN batch size of 64; this addresses a batch-size-related accuracy condition, but does not test the version's fixed-epoch global-batch comparison (R1, R2). The larger group size also increases training time (R3).
